chapter_title: Chương 14: 0014【Khởi hành thôi, lên đường thôi】

segments.title: Chương 14: 0014【Khởi hành thôi, lên đường thôi】
segments.content:
The road at the school gate stretched from east to west.

The two of them planned to travel in opposite directions.

Bian Guanyue looked puzzled, and for once, spoke a long sentence: "Are we waiting for the bus here? When I come back from Rongcheng, I always go to the city center first, then take a bus to the county's East Bus Station."

Chen Guiliang explained, "The school is in the northeast of the county, and the East Bus Station is in the southeast. If we take the route you mentioned, we'd have to take a bus from here, cross the entire county, and then transfer to another bus. Once we get to the city, we'd have to cross half of it again to reach the computer repair shop."

"Oh." Bian Guanyue didn't ask any more questions.

Everything Chen Guiliang said was true, he just hadn't told the whole truth.

The route Bian Guanyue usually took was all urban roads and provincial highways, where the driving speed was certainly much faster.

The route Chen Guiliang chose, however, was a rugged and uneven county road for the entire journey.

There was no way to go fast even if they wanted to!

The distances of the two routes were similar, but the county road took more than three times as long as the provincial highway, because rural buses often made stops along the way.

In her confusion, Bian Guanyue boarded a rural bus.

The dilapidated state of the bus was enough to make her temporarily forget her sorrow...

Half of the windows were broken; they either couldn't be opened or closed properly, or the entire pane of glass was missing. Many others were shattered and held together with clear tape.

The seats were long benches arranged in rows, with frames made of iron pipes and cushions and backrests of faux leather.

Due to prolonged use, the leather cushions and backrests were covered in holes of all sizes. In some places, the sponge inside had been pulled out, and a few seats were just empty iron frames.

There were better-conditioned rural buses, but those good ones didn't run the full route, only willing to cover the busiest sections with the most passengers.

"Can this bus even run properly?" Bian Guanyue was dumbfounded.

Chen Guiliang chuckled and said, "This bus isn't much younger than your parents. If you go back four or five years, it even had a giant natural gas bag on the roof."

Bian Guanyue asked, "The bus company doesn't scrap it?"

Chen Guiliang pointed at the driver and the ticket conductor: "It's already been scrapped. But it was sold to them at a low price to run exclusively on rural routes. They don't belong to the bus company; they're private operators who have contracted the rural routes."

While they were talking, the female ticket conductor had already grown impatient, "Where are you going? Hurry up and buy your tickets!"

Chen Guiliang took out 11 yuan, "Two people, to the train station."

It was afternoon, and on a rural route, there were pitifully few passengers.

Besides Chen Guiliang and Bian Guanyue, there were only two farmers on the bus returning to their villages from the county town.

Just as Chen Guiliang was about to find a good seat, the driver slammed on the accelerator as if he were rushing to a funeral.

Bian Guanyue, with her backpack on and a laptop in her arms, was completely unsteady while walking. Her whole body pitched toward the back of the bus.

Chen Guiliang quickly caught her, nearly falling over with her.

Fortunately, he was prepared, his other hand grabbing the backrest of a nearby seat.

To prove his honorable intentions, Chen Guiliang cursed loudly, "Are you trying to kill someone? Driving so fast, can't you see people are still standing!"

The driver didn't respond.

But the female ticket conductor was a tigress, "If you want to ride, then sit. If not, get a refund and get off!"

"I'm going to file a complaint against you!" Chen Guiliang immediately retorted.

Bian Guanyue struggled free from his arms, tugged his sleeve, and pleaded, "Forget it, let's not argue."

Only then did Chen Guiliang quiet down and lead Bian Guanyue to choose seats.

They picked two seats that were in slightly better condition. Bian Guanyue took the window seat, and Chen Guiliang sat by the aisle.

Not long after they had settled down, the driver slammed on the brakes again.

There was a large pothole ahead, and he intended to slow down and go around it.

Bian Guanyue was completely unprepared for this and her body involuntarily lurched forward. Just as she lurched, the driver jerked the steering wheel to swerve around the pothole, and Bian Guanyue was thrown into Chen Guiliang beside her.

"Exciting, isn't it?" Chen Guiliang grinned.

Bian Guanyue couldn't care about anything else and quickly protected the laptop in her arms. She was afraid that with one wrong move, the computer would be completely shaken to pieces before they even reached the city.

After a short distance, the bus's speed became extremely slow.

But the bumping suddenly intensified. Her bottom had just landed back on the seat after being lifted, only to be jolted airborne again.

Bian Guanyue had completely forgotten her sadness. One hand clutched the laptop tightly, the other gripped the rusty iron bar of the seat in front. She complained in frustration, "Why don't they ever fix such a terrible road?"

Chen Guiliang said, "It used to be worse, there wasn't even a cement road. On rainy days with big puddles, and with the windows missing glass, passengers by the window would get splashed with muddy water. When I was in junior high, they finally paved it with cement, but it was ruined after just six months. The broken cement road is even bumpier than the old gravel road."

Seeing the smile on Chen Guiliang's face, Bian Guanyue felt a surge of frustration.

She seriously suspected that Chen Guiliang was doing this on purpose!

If she had known the road conditions here were this bad, Bian Guanyue would have definitely chosen the other route.

Swaying left and right, flying up and down, their bodies bumped into each other from time to time.

Bian Guanyue said nothing, sitting there with her full concentration, as if she were dealing with a war.

Seeing her like this, Chen Guiliang also kept quiet to avoid annoying her.

After a full hour, the bus arrived at a slightly larger market town.

Then, it stopped and didn't move.

The female conductor, holding the ticket box in one arm and gripping the door with the other, leaned half her body out of the bus and yelled at the top of her lungs, "Train station, train station, leaving soon! Train station, train station..."

Seven or eight passengers boarded one after another. Even when there was no one left outside, the conductor kept yelling.

Bian Guanyue asked, "How long will it stop?"

Chen Guiliang recalled carefully, "Usually for about ten minutes. When there are very few passengers, I've seen it stop for over forty minutes. You could fall asleep, wake up, and it still wouldn't have left."

Bian Guanyue had only eaten a few bites for lunch, had a huge fight with her mother, and had been crying secretly ever since, followed by an hour of battling the bus. Now that the bus had stopped, her tension eased, and she started to feel sleepy.

"Hold this for me." Bian Guanyue handed him the laptop.

Chen Guiliang reached out and took it.

Bian Guanyue took an MP3 player out of her backpack, put on the earbuds, and prepared to listen to music.

After just a few lines, she felt it wasn't right.

Chen Guiliang had skipped his afternoon classes just to take her to the city to get her computer fixed. How could she just listen to music and rest, leaving Chen Guiliang by himself?

"You listen." Bian Guanyue offered him the MP3 player.

Chen Guiliang accepted it without any hesitation. After figuring out the left and right earbuds, he promptly put one in his own ear and offered the other to Bian Guanyue's.

Bian Guanyue flinched towards the window; she wasn't used to being so close to people.

"Put it on. Listening to music together won't get you pregnant," Chen Guiliang said, leaving no room for argument.

"I put it on, it won't get you pregnant."

"Sorry, I thought I had it on."

Bian Guanyue had already ducked her head out the window, but Chen Guiliang's hand followed with the earbud.

She couldn't avoid it, and it would be rude to get angry, so she was forced to share a pair of headphones with Chen Guiliang.

"Get some sleep."

Chen Guiliang knew when to quit while he was ahead. He flicked through a few songs on the MP3 player, then leaned back in his seat and pretended to sleep with his eyes closed.

Bian Guanyue looked at the laptop in his lap, wanting to ask for it back several times, but after thinking it over, she felt it wasn't necessary.

She was indeed tired, so Bian Guanyue also closed her eyes.

"Love starts from zero, testing how rational two people can be."

"Only after finding the words written at the very beginning, do I realize how much we loved each other then..."

Stefanie Sun's "Love Starts from Zero" played through the earbuds, and Bian Guanyue's pretty face blushed for no reason.

It was her first time sharing earbuds with a boy to listen to music, and of all things, she heard such ambiguous lyrics.

Wasn't it too much of a coincidence?

Chen Guiliang also thought it was quite a coincidence; he'd found it after skipping only four songs.

Bian Guanyue opened her eyes to peek at Chen Guiliang sleeping beside her. His profile seemed a bit more handsome, making his thin cheeks look less sunken.

"I would never like him. That guy is a total liar, he even has that junior schoolmate wrapped around his finger!"

Bian Guanyue closed her eyes again to rest, but she didn't take out the earbud, continuing to listen to Stefanie Sun's song.

Time passed, second by second.

The female conductor's voice was battle-hardened, and she was still yelling nonstop, "We're leaving, the bus is leaving, get on if you haven't already!"

There was no response; her more than ten minutes of yelling had been for nothing.

The female conductor slammed the bus door shut in a huff and started yelling and cursing at the driver, "Get moving, what are you spacing out for, you turtle's son?"

This driver was most likely her husband, destined to spend his life traversing the treacherous mountains of Shu.

The driver said nothing and abruptly slammed on the accelerator.

A passenger fell backward, his head hitting the iron bar of the backrest. He immediately cursed, "Does this turtle's son even know how to drive?"

"What the hell are you yelling about, you son of a bitch?" the female conductor shot back instantly, and the bus filled with the sound of their curses.

Both had explosive tempers and foul mouths.

Bian Guanyue was half-asleep and half-awake. She was completely unaware of the driver's sudden start and also fell backward.

But she didn't hit the rusty iron bar of the backrest. Instead, she hit Chen Guiliang's palm. Her helpful deskmate had used his hand to block her.

Startled awake, Bian Guanyue understood what had happened and quickly turned to look at Chen Guiliang.

Chen Guiliang pulled his hand back and said with a smile, "No need to thank me. Helping others for the joy of it, seeking no reward, is what we Red Scarf pioneers should do."

Bian Guanyue didn't know whether to laugh or cry. She turned her face toward the window, the corners of her mouth curling up slightly.

Not long after passing the town, the bus went wild again.

Bian Guanyue couldn't sleep at all. Since Chen Guiliang was holding the computer for her, she could now grip the iron bar of the front seat with both hands.

Just as they finally passed the bumpy section and Bian Guanyue let her guard down, the bus made a sharp turn that threw her off balance, and she collided heavily with Chen Guiliang.

Bian Guanyue couldn't take it anymore and finally voiced the question in her mind, "Are you doing this on purpose?"

Chen Guiliang looked innocent, "The driver's driving, what does it have to do with me?"

Bian Guanyue said, "You chose this road on purpose!"

"I always take this road. I'm not familiar with the one by the East Bus Station," Chen Guiliang denied it to the death.

As they spoke, the driver slammed on the brakes; someone was waving on the side of the road.

There were no bus stops on rural roads; people could be picked up anywhere, anytime.

"Ah!"

"Driver, please slow down!"

Bian Guanyue slammed her forehead against the iron bar of the seat in front, leaving a red mark.

She was about to go crazy.

Chen Guiliang, delighting in her misfortune, almost burst out laughing.

The normally cold and aloof ice queen who usually spoke in two- or three-word sentences. Look how lively and outgoing she had become now, even taking the initiative to greet the driver.

This bus ride was only halfway through, but it was guaranteed to be an unforgettable experience for Bian Guanyue for the rest of her life.

It was a form of the misattribution of arousal effect. All those books Chen Guiliang read hadn't been for nothing.
